articles.body: In a small accounting practice there's a monthly job nobody likes. Before the books can close, someone has to chase clients for what's missing: the invoice behind a payment, the receipt for a card charge, the bank statement that never got sent. I've been on the other side of it too. My own accountant chases me to confirm invoices on e-fatura, the Portuguese tax authority's invoice portal, and I'm exactly the kind of client who answers late. This year the chase started turning into a software feature. What moved Xero announced "Document Requests" in its Partner Hub on 20 August. Its AI agent, JAX, will "request documents from the client, send reminders … then match it with transactions in Xero" .

articles.excerpt: The first time someone mentioned WebMCP to me, I assumed it was a diagnostics tool for web apps. The name sounds like something you would open next to the network tab. My second guess was worse: I tho…
articles.body: The first time someone mentioned WebMCP to me, I assumed it was a diagnostics tool for web apps. The name sounds like something you would open next to the network tab. My second guess was worse: I thought maybe it was a Playwright alternative. Luckily, I was wrong both times, and figuring out why is how I ended up adding it to salih.dev (where probably nobody would use). A few months ago I wrote about building an agent-friendly personal website with specs . The site serves Markdown to agents, has an llms.txt , and answers a set of .well-known discovery files. One of those files was /.well-known/webmcp.json , and it said, politely, that there were no browser tools here. In case you don't know me, I am a very open person, if I don't have something, I would say "I don't have it".

articles.title: VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported said yes to H.265, but each browser meant something different
articles.excerpt: For my graduation project I'm building a small page that re-encodes lecture clips in the browser, and I wanted an H.265 option because the files come out smaller. The WebCodecs docs make the check loo…
articles.body: For my graduation project I'm building a small page that re-encodes lecture clips in the browser, and I wanted an H.265 option because the files come out smaller. The WebCodecs docs make the check look like one line: pass a config to VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported() and read supported . I wrote a probe, ran it in six browser builds on my Mac, and the answers looked tidy until I actually encoded with them. A true turned out to mean at least three different things. What finally let me tell them apart was boring: encode the same 30 frames under every hint and put the byte counts and times next to each other. I tested six browser builds on one Mac Everything ran on an Apple M4 with macOS 26.5 on 2026-10-19.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan Explanation: This is an unusual rainbow. For one thing, the rainbow is not complete, appearing only in a sunlit fan — but that by itself is not very unusual. What is most unusual is the fake location of the Sun . The Sun appears to be toward the front, just below those hills — but it is not. That is not how rainbows work . Rainbows involve a backward reflection from falling rain , so that the Sun must really be behind you .

articles.excerpt: Games where choices matter often narrow what matters to character death or branching endings. These narrative-driven games do it differently
articles.body: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? Typically, we think it's a good use of branching narratives when you have a properly big, dramatic effect on how things play out or when you have hundreds of endings. Just look at how so much attention on Baldur's Gate 3 focused on its endings or, years before, how everyone tended to ignore the smaller ways the Mass Effect trilogy changed across three games in favor of looking at the restrictive outcomes in Mass Effect 3 .

articles.body: President Donald Trump announced this afternoon that Elon Musk's SpaceX shares for children will be given through Trump Accounts. Musk said earlier today that he would give one of his SpaceX shares to "every kid in America" sometime next year. articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
